newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania experimental bomb explodes, kills 15.
newsitem.headline: Romania experimental bomb explodes, kills 15.

text.p: An experimental shrapnel bomb exploded on Wednesday during a test at a military airfield in southern Romania, killing 15 workers and injuring three more, one seriously, a senior government official said.

Constantin Dudu Ionescu, State Secretary for Defence, told a government briefing in Bucharest that the experimental bomb had detonated on Wednesday afternoon at the airfield in Craiova, 235 km (140 miles) west of the capital.
He said the dead included eight defence industry workers and seven military engineers. One person was taken to hospital in a coma and two others suffered lesser injuries.
"We cannot say what caused the accident, but we suspect there could have been a technical reason," he said.
Ionescu described the device as an "experimental shrapnel bomb" produced at the Mija defence plant in Ploiesti, north of Bucharest.
"Tests will continue as this is one of the most modern types of ammunition we have," he said.

A defence ministry statement, quoted by the official Rompres news agency, said the test was being conducted as part of procedures to secure a licence for the device, described as "a new type of aviation ammunition".
A IAR-93 training plane which was carrying the device on the tarmac was destroyed in the blast.
A government commission was dispatched to Craiova to investigate the causes of the explosion.
